changelog: Replace C2 (Cohesion) to allow and prefer internal cuts inside noun groups when the left fragment is a clear identifiable head and the right only adds modifiers, addressing the primary finding that the prompt overgeneralizes 'don't cut inside long noun groups' and needs denser short-latency segmentation.
findings: The prompt underestimates scope-bearing material that appears immediately after a cut (quantifiers, negation, rescoping adverbials, contrastive coordinators, or disambiguating head verbs/nouns) and so ranks cuts before those words too high.

The prompt overgeneralizes "don't cut inside long noun groups" and thus avoids dense internal cuts that short-latency segmentation needs even when the left fragment remains an identifiable head and the right only adds modifiers or clarifiers.

edits.was: - Cohesion: If the left and right sides are translated independently and then co
edits.now: - Cohesion: When left and right pieces are translated separately and concatenate

diagnosis.why: The revised cohesion wording made the model more willing to place internal cuts that separate identifiable heads from their modifiers, which raised H_set for very short-latency pieces (≤3 words and some gains up to ≤10) but also induced new spurious splits (e.g., breaking predicates or fragmenting enumerations) that produced many degraded mid-length examples; the net effect is therefore small and inconclusive.
diagnosis.lesson: A later revision should keep the gain in very-short (≤3-word) internal segmentation while avoiding a new bias that cuts apart predicates or fragments enumerations and mid-length pieces.
